# Vestra Player SDK

> @vestra-player/sdk 1.5.11: write plugins for Vestra Player in TypeScript (plugin API `vestra/1`). A plugin is a folder with `manifest.json` and an entry module whose default export `activate(plugin)` the player calls; it runs in its own Node.js process. llms-full.txt, next to this file, has every declaration, the guides and the examples; L<n> below are its line numbers.

**How plugins run**

- Each plugin runs in its own Node.js process (Node.js 26, which the player ships) started by the player.
- The player loads the entry module and calls its **default export** `activate(plugin)`.
- Everything a plugin creates (commands, windows, panels, filters, listeners…) is a handle owned by `plugin` or a child scope, and is released automatically when the plugin stops.
- Plugins are trusted code.
- The API is the same on macOS and Windows.

**Rules**

- **Only the public SDK.** Import `@vestra-player/sdk` with `import type` only (a runtime import fails `vestra-plugin build`) and `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` only in tests. `@vestra-player/sdk/runtime` and the SDK's internal modules are for the player.
- **No other plugins.** Do not import another plugin's code, read its directory or data directory, or talk to it privately (shared files, sockets, messages). A plugin must load, run and stop while no other plugin is installed. Plugins share only what the API makes public: player state, timeline marks, menus, settings pages.
- **No system commands.** Do not run `open`, `sips`, `plutil`, `security`, `cmd`, `powershell` or similar. Use the API (`plugin.system` to open files and links, `plugin.clipboard`, `plugin.secrets`, `plugin.tools` for ffmpeg and ffprobe) or portable Node.js code. If the API lacks something every system needs, ask for it in the SDK repository.
- **macOS and Windows.** The same code runs on both: build paths with `node:path`, write package paths with `/`, and handle `unsupported` where a method documents a platform difference.
- **Your own id.** `<owner>.<name>`, where the owner is your GitHub user or organization. `vestra` and `vestra.*` are reserved for the plugins built into the player.

**Files**

```text
my-plugin/
  manifest.json        identity and capabilities
  main.ts              the entry module
  ui/hello.slint       optional: user interface
  tests/main.test.ts   tests (node:test)
  package.json         dev dependency and scripts
```

**manifest.json** (every field; unknown fields and capabilities are rejected; id ≤ 128 bytes, name, author ≤ 64 characters, punchline ≤ 120, description ≤ 2000, tags ≤ 8 of ≤ 24 characters, license ≤ 64, sourceUrl ≤ 2048 bytes, icon PNG or JPEG ≤ 512 KB and 1024 px per side, readme, changelog ≤ 256 KB)

```json
{
  "id": "me.hello",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.osd"],
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.4.1",
  "name": "Hello",
  "author": "Me",
  "punchline": "Says hello from the Tools menu.",
  "description": "A first plugin.\nIt adds Tools ▸ Hello, which shows an on-screen message.",
  "tags": ["example"],
  "icon": "assets/icon.png",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "changelog": "CHANGELOG.md",
  "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/me/hello",
  "license": "MIT"
}
```

**main.ts**

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "hello",
    path: ["Tools", "Hello"],
    run: () => plugin.osd.show("Hello"),
  });
}
```

**Capabilities** (a call without its capability fails with `capability`)

- `commands`: `commands.add`, `host.run`
- `ui.window`: `windows.create`
- `ui.mount`: `panels.mount`, `panels.bottom` / `.sidebar` / `.backdrop`
- `ui.dialog`: `dialogs.*`
- `ui.osd`: `osd.show`, `osd.panel`
- `ui.drop`: `drops.provide`, `Panel.onDrop`
- `ui.theme`: `appearance.set`
- `ui.settings`: `settings.page`, `settings.show`
- `playback.read`: reading `player.state` at start, `refresh`, `stats`, `chapters`, `audioDevices`, `timeline.marks`
- `events`: live `player.state` / `onChange`, panel visibility, subtitle and window updates
- `playback.control`: `player.open`, `setPaused`, `seek`, `setRate`, … and `power.preventSleep`
- `producer.av`: `player.openStream` (with `playback.control`: the stream becomes the player's source)
- `processing.video`: `video.filter` (with `playback.read` and `events`), `video.view`, `video.render` (with `playback.read`)
- `processing.audio`: `audio.filter` (with `playback.read` and `events`)
- `subtitles.read` / `subtitles.control`: reading / changing subtitles
- `media.read` / `media.control`: `media.capture`, snapshot exports
- `source.resolve`: `resolvers.add`
- `plugins.manage`: `packages.validate`, `rollback`, `setEnabled`, `uninstall`
- `clipboard`: `clipboard.*`
- `window.control`: `window.setVideoArea`, `setAlwaysOnTop`, `setCursorAutoHide`, `setPictureInPicture`
- `bindings.manage`: `bindings.*`
- `timeline.marks`: `timeline.layer()`
- `secrets`: `secrets.*`
- No capability is needed for `tools`, `storage`, `system`, `ui.image`, `plugin.app`, reading `window.state` and `appearance.theme`, and `packages.list`.

**Test** (`tests/*.test.ts`, run by `vestra-plugin test`)

```ts
// tests/main.test.ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("shows the position", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url), // reads manifest.json
  });
  host.setSource({ phase: "ready", position: 12, duration: 60 });
  await host.settle();
  await host.command("where").run();
  assert.deepEqual(host.osd, ["12.0 s of 60.0 s"]);
  await stop();
});
```

**Command line**

- `vestra-plugin check [dir...]`: Checks the manifest, then a strict type check of the plugin and its tests.
- `vestra-plugin test [dir...]`: Runs `node --test` on `tests/*.test.{ts,mjs}`.
- `vestra-plugin build [dir...] [--version x.y.z]`: Writes `dist/`: types stripped, files copied, manifest versioned.
- `vestra-plugin pack [dir...] [--version x.y.z] [--out dir]`: Builds, then packs `dist/` as `<id>-<version>.vxp`.
- `vestra-plugin i18n extract [dir...] [--locale lang]`: Collects the texts to translate into `locales/`, keeping translations.
- `vestra-plugin i18n check [dir...]`: Translation coverage and untranslatable text (warnings only).
- `vestra-player --plugin <dir>` runs a plugin from source, no build needed.

**Error codes** (`error.code`; branch on it, never on `message`)

- `stale`: A condition no longer held
- `capability`: The manifest does not declare the capability the call needs
- `invalid`: A bad argument
- `missing`: The target does not exist
- `busy`: The player is still doing a previous call of the same kind
- `conflict`: Another plugin owns the resource, or this plugin already uses the id
- `unavailable`: Not possible right now
- `unsupported`: Not possible on this system, build or source
- `failed`: The operation ran and failed
- `aborted`: An `AbortSignal` fired
- `timeout`: A time limit ran out
- `limit`: A player-wide limit was reached, a property value is over the limits of PropValue, or a request is longer than the player's 1 MiB message
- `reserved`: Packages.validate, PackageCandidate.install: the id is `vestra` or starts with `vestra.`, which only the player's built-in plugins use
- `versionMismatch`: The package needs a newer player or another `apiVersion`
- `ui-prepare`: The player could not prepare a mounted panel or a settings page
- `ui`: The player could not apply a property to a tool window or a settings page, or could not build the Options window
- `disabled`: The plugin is being stopped
- Others: PluginError, llms-full.txt L974.

## Examples

Complete plugins with tests, in [examples/](https://github.com/vestrasys/vestra-player-sdk/tree/main/examples) and in llms-full.txt:

- hello: The README Quick start: one menu command and an on-screen message. L5954–6043
- blur: A tool window with one slider that blurs the playing video. L6044–6305
- signal-generator: Generates its own video and audio: colour bars and a 1 kHz tone. L6306–6638
- bookmark: A tool window bound to the playback state: remember the position and jump back to it. L6639–6823
- panel-menu: A sidebar panel with its own right-click menu. L6824–7029
- menus: Radio menu items, separator groups and a menu item whose title changes. L7030–7189
- theme-widgets: A tool window drawn with the player's theme and widgets. L7190–7353
- markdown: A window that shows a Markdown document. L7354–7547
- i18n: A plugin in the player's language: English source text, a Chinese translation. L7548–7715
